paper_title: Limits on the evolutionary rates of biological traits (García-Pintos, 2024, Scientific Reports)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
The general Price rate limit is not only an upper bound but a sharp projection theorem. At any fixed differentiability time, define
\[
R_A:=\frac{d\langle A\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot A\rangle .
\]
If \(\sigma_A\sigma_r>0\), then
\[
R_A=\sigma_A\sigma_r\rho_{A,r},\qquad -1\leq \rho_{A,r}\leq 1,
\]
where \(\rho_{A,r}\) is the weighted correlation between the centered trait and centered growth rate. Since \(\sigma_r^2=I_F\),
\[
|R_A|\leq \sigma_A\sqrt{I_F}.
\]
For fixed \(\sigma_A=s>0\), the largest possible value of \(|R_A|\) over all trait coordinates with that standard deviation is exactly \(s\sigma_r=s\sqrt{I_F}\). Equality holds exactly when the centered trait is proportional to the centered growth-rate vector on the support of \(p\). If \(\sigma_A\sigma_r=0\), then \(R_A=0\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
(P1)\quad &\mathcal J\text{ is finite},\quad p_j>0,\quad \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j=1.\\
(P2)\quad &\langle X\rangle:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_jx_j,\quad
\sigma_X^2:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(x_j-\langle X\rangle)^2.\\
(P3)\quad &R_A=\operatorname{cov}(A,r)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(r_j-\langle r\rangle).\\
(P4)\quad &I_F=\sigma_r^2.\\
(P5)\quad &\left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_ju_jv_j\right|^2
\leq \left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_ju_j^2\right)\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_jv_j^2\right),
\end{align*}
with equality in \((P5)\) exactly when the vectors \((u_j)\) and \((v_j)\) are linearly dependent on the support of \(p\).

\section*{Derivation}
Assume first that \(\sigma_A\sigma_r>0\). Define
\begin{align*}
\rho_{A,r}
&:=\frac{\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(r_j-\langle r\rangle)}{\sigma_A\sigma_r}.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
R_A
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(r_j-\langle r\rangle) &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\sigma_A\sigma_r\rho_{A,r}. &&\text{by the definition of }\rho_{A,r}
\end{align*}
Moreover,
\begin{align*}
|\rho_{A,r}|^2
&=\frac{\left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(r_j-\langle r\rangle)\right|^2}{\sigma_A^2\sigma_r^2}\\
&\leq \frac{\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)^2\right)
\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(r_j-\langle r\rangle)^2\right)}{\sigma_A^2\sigma_r^2} &&\text{by }(P5)\\
&=1. &&\text{by }(P2)
\end{align*}
Thus \(-1\leq \rho_{A,r}\leq 1\), and
\begin{align*}
|R_A|
&\leq \sigma_A\sigma_r &&\text{because }|\rho_{A,r}|\leq 1\\
&=\sigma_A\sqrt{I_F}. &&\text{by }(P4)
\end{align*}
For sharpness, fix \(s>0\) and set
\[
a_j:=c+s\frac{r_j-\langle r\rangle}{\sigma_r}
\]
with arbitrary constant \(c\). Then \(\langle A\rangle=c\), \(\sigma_A=s\), and
\begin{align*}
R_A
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\left(s\frac{r_j-\langle r\rangle}{\sigma_r}\right)(r_j-\langle r\rangle)\\
&=s\sigma_r.
\end{align*}
Changing the sign of the centered term gives \(R_A=-s\sigma_r\), so the supremum of \(|R_A|\) is exactly \(s\sigma_r\). Equality in the bound is exactly the equality case of weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, namely
\[
a_j-\langle A\rangle=\lambda(r_j-\langle r\rangle)
\]
for some real \(\lambda\) on the support of \(p\). If \(\sigma_A=0\) or \(\sigma_r=0\), the covariance in \((P3)\) is zero by the same Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle R_A=\sigma_A\sigma_r\rho_{A,r},\qquad |R_A|\leq \sigma_A\sqrt{I_F},\qquad
\sup_{\sigma_A=s}|R_A|=s\sqrt{I_F}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_2:
\section*{Claim}
For mutation-free replicator dynamics, centered fitness is the unique steepest direction for changing trait averages. Suppose
\[
\dot p_j=p_j(f_j-\langle f\rangle),\qquad \sigma_f>0.
\]
For every trait \(A\), the population-frequency contribution to the trait-average rate is
\[
R_A:=\frac{d\langle A\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot A\rangle=\operatorname{cov}(A,f).
\]
Among all traits with fixed standard deviation \(\sigma_A=s\), the maximum possible value of \(|R_A|\) is exactly \(s\sigma_f\), attained exactly when the centered trait is proportional to centered fitness. In particular, taking \(A=f\) gives
\[
\frac{d\langle f\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot f\rangle=\sigma_f^2,
\]
so Fisher's variance identity is the unnormalised steepest-direction case.

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
(P1)\quad &\mathcal J\text{ is finite},\quad p_j>0,
\quad \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j=1.\\
(P2)\quad &\dot p_j=p_j(f_j-\langle f\rangle).\\
(P3)\quad &R_A=\frac{d\langle A\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot A\rangle=\operatorname{cov}(A,f).\\
(P4)\quad &\operatorname{cov}(A,f)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(f_j-\langle f\rangle).\\
(P5)\quad &\sigma_X^2=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(x_j-\langle X\rangle)^2.\\
(P6)\quad &\left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_ju_jv_j\right|^2
\leq \left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_ju_j^2\right)\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_jv_j^2\right),
\end{align*}
with equality exactly when \((u_j)\) and \((v_j)\) are linearly dependent on the support of \(p\).

\section*{Derivation}
For any trait \(A\),
\begin{align*}
|R_A|^2
&=|\operatorname{cov}(A,f)|^2 &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\left|\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)(f_j-\langle f\rangle)\right|^2 &&\text{by }(P4)\\
&\leq \left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle)^2\right)
\left(\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j(f_j-\langle f\rangle)^2\right) &&\text{by }(P6)\\
&=\sigma_A^2\sigma_f^2. &&\text{by }(P5)
\end{align*}
Hence \(|R_A|\leq \sigma_A\sigma_f\). If \(\sigma_A=s\), then \(|R_A|\leq s\sigma_f\). To show this is sharp, choose
\[
a_j:=c+s\frac{f_j-\langle f\rangle}{\sigma_f}
\]
with arbitrary constant \(c\). Then \(\langle A\rangle=c\), \(\sigma_A=s\), and
\begin{align*}
R_A
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\left(s\frac{f_j-\langle f\rangle}{\sigma_f}\right)(f_j-\langle f\rangle)\\
&=s\sigma_f.
\end{align*}
Changing the sign of the centered term gives \(R_A=-s\sigma_f\), so
\[
\sup_{\sigma_A=s}|R_A|=s\sigma_f.
\]
The equality condition in \((P6)\) gives the exact attaining traits:
\[
a_j-\langle A\rangle=\lambda(f_j-\langle f\rangle)
\]
for some real \(\lambda\) on the support of \(p\). Finally, set \(A=f\). Then \(a_j=f_j\), so
\begin{align*}
\frac{d\langle f\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot f\rangle
&=\operatorname{cov}(f,f) &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\sigma_f^2. &&\text{by }(P5)
\end{align*}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \sup_{\sigma_A=s}\left|\frac{d\langle A\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot A\rangle\right|=s\sigma_f,
\qquad
\frac{d\langle f\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot f\rangle=\sigma_f^2}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
The deterministic replicator-mutator rate limit contains a sharper conditional-variance structure. Let
\[
\dot p_j=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}f_k-p_j\langle f\rangle,
\qquad
\mu_j:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj},
\qquad
b_k:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}a_j.
\]
Define the corrected residual
\[
R_A:=\frac{d\langle A\rangle}{dt}-\langle \dot A\rangle-
\langle f\rangle(\langle A\rangle_\mu-\langle A\rangle).
\]
Then
\[
R_A=\operatorname{cov}_p(f,b),
\qquad |R_A|\leq \sigma_f\sigma_b\leq \sigma_f\sigma_{A,\mu},
\]
where
\[
\sigma_b^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sigma_{A,\mu}^2=\sigma_b^2+\eta_A,
\qquad
\eta_A:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}(a_j-b_k)^2\geq 0.
\]
Thus the paper's \(\sigma_{A,\mu}\sigma_f\) bound is conservative exactly by the within-parent mutation variance \(\eta_A\); the selection-sensitive part depends only on the variance across parent types of the post-mutation conditional trait mean \(b_k\).

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
(P1)\quad &\mathcal J\text{ is finite},\quad p_k>0,
\quad \sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k=1.\\
(P2)\quad &Q_{kj}\geq0,
\quad \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}=1\text{ for every }k.\\
(P3)\quad &\mu_j:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj},
\quad b_k:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}a_j.\\
(P4)\quad &\langle A\rangle_\mu:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mu_ja_j,
\quad \langle f\rangle:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kf_k.\\
(P5)\quad &\sigma_{A,\mu}^2:=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mu_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2,
\quad \sigma_f^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(f_k-\langle f\rangle)^2.\\
(P6)\quad &R_A=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(f_k-\langle f\rangle)(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu).\\
(P7)\quad &\left|\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_ku_kv_k\right|^2
\leq \left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_ku_k^2\right)\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kv_k^2\right).
\end{align*}

\section*{Derivation}
First,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kb_k
&=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}a_j &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}\right)a_j &&\text{finite sums}\\
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mu_ja_j &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\langle A\rangle_\mu. &&\text{by }(P4)
\end{align*}
Therefore \((P6)\) can be written as
\begin{align*}
R_A
&=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(f_k-\langle f\rangle)(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)\\
&=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kf_kb_k-
\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kf_k\right)
\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_kb_k\right)\\
&=\operatorname{cov}_p(f,b).
\end{align*}
Applying weighted Cauchy--Schwarz,
\begin{align*}
|R_A|^2
&\leq \left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(f_k-\langle f\rangle)^2\right)
\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2\right) &&\text{by }(P7)\\
&=\sigma_f^2\sigma_b^2, &&\text{by definitions}
\end{align*}
so \(|R_A|\leq\sigma_f\sigma_b\). It remains to compare \(\sigma_b\) with \(\sigma_{A,\mu}\). Since \(a_j-\langle A\rangle_\mu=(a_j-b_k)+(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)\),
\begin{align*}
\sigma_{A,\mu}^2
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mu_j(a_j-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2 &&\text{by }(P5)\\
&=\sum_{k,j\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}(a_j-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2 &&\text{by }(P3)\\
&=\sum_{k,j\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}\left((a_j-b_k)+(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)\right)^2\\
&=\sum_{k,j\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}(a_j-b_k)^2
+\sum_{k,j\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2\\
&\quad +2\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)
\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}(a_j-b_k).
\end{align*}
For each \(k\),
\begin{align*}
\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}(a_j-b_k)
&=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}a_j-b_k\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}\\
&=b_k-b_k=0. &&\text{by }(P2)\text{ and }(P3)
\end{align*}
Also,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{k,j\in\mathcal J}p_kQ_{kj}(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2
&=\sum_{k\in\mathcal J}p_k(b_k-\langle A\rangle_\mu)^2\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}Q_{kj}\\
&=\sigma_b^2. &&\text{by }(P2)
\end{align*}
Thus
\[
\sigma_{A,\mu}^2=\sigma_b^2+\eta_A,
\]
where \(\eta_A\geq0\) by definition as a sum of nonnegative terms. Hence \(\sigma_b\leq\sigma_{A,\mu}\), and
\[
|R_A|\leq \sigma_f\sigma_b\leq \sigma_f\sigma_{A,\mu}.
\]

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle R_A=\operatorname{cov}_p(f,b),\qquad
|R_A|\leq\sigma_f\sigma_b,\qquad
\sigma_{A,\mu}^2=\sigma_b^2+\eta_A\geq\sigma_b^2}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_metadata.revision_intent: Improve alignment by keeping all deeper proofs inside the paper's four stated rate-limit goals while strengthening scientific value through sharpness, variational optimality, variance decomposition, and stochastic force-budget inversion.

rubric_interpretation.top_level_schema: Exactly paper_title, contiguous deeper_reasoning_k string fields, and one deeper_metadata object.
rubric_interpretation.latex_constraint: Each reasoning entry must compile under article with amsmath and amssymb only.
rubric_interpretation.deeper_value_constraint: Entries should be proof-like extensions of the core reasoning, not paraphrases of the source paper or metadata audits.

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Sharp Price covariance bound, equality cases, and Fisher-information rate budget
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: Preserves the finite-population Price identity and covariance rate-limit target while adding the exact extremal structure of the Cauchy-Schwarz step.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Identifies which trait coordinates can actually attain the maximum rate and interprets Fisher information as the available population-frequency speed budget.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Converts the generic inequality into an attainable supremum theorem over fixed-variance traits.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: Sharp; equality holds iff centered trait and centered growth-rate coordinates are proportional on the support.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids merely restating the Price equation by proving attainability and degeneracy cases.
controlled_external_lemmas: weighted Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and equality condition
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Requires positive support for division and equality statements; the proof explicitly handles zero-variance degeneracies.

deeper_reasoning_2.title: Variational steepest-direction theorem for natural selection
deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: Uses exactly the mutation-free replicator residual specified in G1 and adds a maximisation theorem over possible trait coordinates.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Shows that fitness is not just a special substitution but the extremal direction of fastest mean-trait change.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Derives a supremum over all fixed-variance traits and identifies the equality class.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: Sharp for every fixed trait standard deviation when sigma_f is nonzero.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Does not duplicate the natural-selection bound; it explains why the fitness special case is the extremal case.
controlled_external_lemmas: weighted Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and equality condition
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Assumes nonzero fitness variance for the normalised maximiser; the zero-variance case collapses to zero residual.

deeper_reasoning_3.title: Conditional-variance sharpening of the replicator-mutator bound
deeper_reasoning_3.goal_alignment: Retains the G2 corrected residual and mutation-driven distribution, but proves a tighter intermediate sigma_b bound before recovering the paper's sigma_A,mu bound.
deeper_reasoning_3.scientific_payoff: Separates variation in conditional post-mutation means, which can couple to fitness, from within-parent mutation variance, which only loosens the published bound.
deeper_reasoning_3.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Adds a law-of-total-variance decomposition hidden inside the Jensen step of the core proof.
deeper_reasoning_3.formal_sharpness: Sharper than the paper-level bound whenever within-parent mutation variance is positive.
deeper_reasoning_3.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids merely reproducing the replicator-mutator inequality by exposing the exact variance lost in the final relaxation.
deeper_reasoning_3.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Introduces b_k as an auxiliary conditional mean, but all quantities are algebraically determined by p, Q, and a from G2.

deeper_reasoning_4.title: Stochastic force-budget inversion and quantitative dominance shares
deeper_reasoning_4.goal_alignment: Uses the exact G3 total integrated bound and regime-decomposition terms rather than adding a new stochastic model or a new drift term.
deeper_reasoning_4.scientific_payoff: Turns the three additive upper-bound terms into necessary lower-bound certificates for selection, mutation, and drift contributions.
deeper_reasoning_4.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Derives residual-gap lower bounds and normalised dominance shares from the paper's total inequality.
deeper_reasoning_4.formal_sharpness: Sharp as an algebraic consequence of the additive bound; no extra stochastic assumption is introduced beyond G3.
deeper_reasoning_4.low_value_rejection_audit: Replaces the previous more external effective-noise refinement with a proof that stays closer to the paper's stated stochastic regime objective.
deeper_reasoning_4.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The inverse lower bounds are necessary certificates rather than sufficient causal identification; metadata states this as force-budget inversion, not empirical attribution.
